limits: Only one CE application process is coordinated; other applications and direct database writers are not.
Reads bypass coordination, but database locks and processing load may delay them. Application graph writes wait during native analysis and extension calculation.
No 100-million-edge benchmark, Enterprise integration, hard database-memory bound, or real lost-commit-acknowledgement fault injection is claimed.
One active schema bundle supports multiple managed kinds. Existing producers cannot be removed or reassigned through uploads.
Schema records, indexes and kind catalog preparation are separate from the all-or-nothing helper, edge and run-record changes.
On an uncertain commit, further writes stop until the operator inspects the run record and restarts the application.
The registry restart was tested on Neo4j; PostgreSQL OpenGraph changes used separate native upload jobs after the mixed-file accounting failure.
